entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Mallius Maximus was a Roman politician and general who rose to prominence during the late Roman Republic. His military campaigns against the Cimbri in modern-day Germany showcased his strategic prowess, while his leadership of the Italian legions played a key role in the Battle of Aquae Sextiae in 102 BCE.

A close ally of Lucius Cornelius Sulla, Maximus served as a senator and later as a military commander under Julius Caesar. His relationship with Caesar was complex, marked by periods of tension and loyalty.

Despite his significant contributions to Roman politics and warfare, Maximus's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries. Nevertheless, his life and achievements continue to be studied by historians seeking to understand the complexities of late Republican Rome.

In conclusion, Gnaeus Mallius Maximus was a pivotal figure in the tumultuous world of late Roman politics and warfare, whose impact can still be felt today.
